# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

**Governing Policy:** 2026 Evolent Clinical Guidelines - Musculoskeletal Surgery (https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2026-05/2026%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines.pdf)

**RE: Appeal of Denial – Reference Number POC-1ACF427871-17933**
**Member:** Casey Iverson
**Member ID:** W207784190
**Plan:** Fidelis Care (Commercial/ACA), New York
**Date of Denial Notice:** 2026-08-25
**Requested Service:** Partial knee replacement (CPT 27446)

To Whom It May Concern:

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for a partial knee replacement (CPT 27446). My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking the plan to reconsider its decision.

## Why I am appealing

The denial notice states that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." However, when I reviewed the criteria the plan cited in support of this denial, I found that the specific clinical criteria listed all pertain to **cervical spine fusion procedures** (Anterior Cervical Discectomy with Fusion, Cervical Posterior Decompression with Fusion, and Cervical Fusion for Axial Neck Pain) — for example, criteria involving "Upper extremity weakness," "Hoffmann sign," "cervical radiculopathy or myelopathy," and imaging of the cervical spine. These criteria concern the neck and spinal cord, not the knee joint.

I am requesting this procedure for a **partial knee replacement**, not a cervical spine fusion. I am not able to find, in the materials provided to me, any plan criteria that address partial knee replacement or knee imaging findings. I want to be clear and transparent: I am not quoting the plan's knee-replacement criteria here because I have not been given that language. I am asking the plan to identify and apply the correct medical necessity criteria for CPT 27446, and to explain how those specific criteria — not the cervical spine criteria referenced in my denial — apply to my case.

## The clinical evidence in my case

While I wait for the plan to clarify which criteria actually govern this request, I want to lay out the relevant facts from my medical record, which I believe support the medical necessity of this surgery:

- **Symptom duration:** I have had 24 months of progressive knee pain that is not relieved by rest.
- **Conservative treatment already tried:**
  - Supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion — 8 weeks, 16 visits completed, from 2026-05-14 to 2026-07-09, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
  - NSAIDs for 4 months, with inadequate relief.
  - A corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-03, which gave only 4 weeks of partial relief.
- **Imaging:** An MRI of my knee on 2026-07-30 showed full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 changes medially.
- **Functional impact:** I cannot climb stairs without assistance, and I wake 3–4 times a night because of pain.
- **Exam findings:** Positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.
- **No disqualifying factors:** No active infection, no untreated substance use; my BMI is 29 and I do not smoke.

My surgeon has reviewed this history and imaging and has documented that partial knee replacement is medically necessary for me.

## What I am asking

I am asking Fidelis Care to:

1. Reconsider the denial of CPT 27446 for partial knee replacement;
2. Identify the specific plan medical necessity criteria that actually apply to partial knee replacement (rather than the cervical spine fusion criteria referenced in my denial notice); and
3. Review the clinical evidence above — including my imaging, my failed conservative treatment, and my functional limitations — against those correct criteria.

I have included this appeal within the time frame stated in my denial notice, which must be received by **2027-02-21**. I understand this can be submitted online at ambetterhealth.com (selecting New York and the appeal/grievance form), by calling the number on my member ID card, or by mail to the appeal address printed on my denial letter.

Please let me know if any additional records or forms are needed to complete this review. I can be reached at [phone number] or [email address].

Thank you for reconsidering my request.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Casey Iverson
Member ID: W207784190
Date: [date]

[Mailing address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*

quotes: Cervical Fusion for Treatment of Axial Neck Pain Criteria Anterior Cervical Discectomy with Fusion (ACDF) – Multiple Levels When one of the two following criteria are met (1–8):

○ Upper extremity weakness ○ Unsteady gait related to myelopathy/balance or generalized lower extremity weakness ○ Disturbance with coordination ○ Hyperreflexia ○ Hoffmann sign ○ Positive Babinski sign and/or clonus ● Progressive neurological deficit (motor deficit, bowel or bladder dysfunction) with corresponding evidence of spinal cord or nerve root compression on an MRI or CT scan images – immediate surgical evaluation is indicated When ALL of the following criteria are met (6–8):

● Cervical radiculopathy or myelopathy due to ruptured disc, spondylosis, spinal instability, or deformity ● Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months;

preferred for examining bony structures, or in individuals presenting with clinical symptoms or signs inconsistent with MRI findings (e.g., foraminal compression not seen on MRI) As first-line treatment without conservative care measures in the following clinical cases (1,2,6,9):
See Cervical Fusion for Treatment of Axial Neck Pain Criteria Cervical Posterior Decompression with Fusion (CPDF) - Single Level When one of the two following criteria are met (1–8,11):

● Cervical radiculopathy or myelopathy from ruptured disc, spondylosis, spinal instability, or deformity OR documented pseudarthrosis of prior ACDF/Cervical Artificial Disc Replacement (CADR) - one of the most common indications for a Single Level or Multi Levels CPDF is a failed anterior procedure ● Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months;
NOTE - Failure of conservative treatment is defined as one of the following:
○ Lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment;
OR ○ Progression or worsening of symptoms during treatment;

OR ○ Documentation of a medical reason the member is unable to participate in treatment Closure of medical or therapy offices, patient inconvenience, or noncompliance without explanation does not constitute “inability to complete” treatment.
● Imaging studies confirm the presence of spinal cord or spinal nerve root compression (disc herniation or foraminal stenosis) at single level corresponding with the clinical findings.

See Cervical Fusion for Treatment of Axial Neck Pain Criteria Cervical Fusion for Treatment of Axial Neck Pain Fusion In Individuals with Non-Radicular Cervical Pain ALL of the following criteria must be met (14,15):

● Improvement of the symptoms has failed or plateaued, and the residual symptoms of pain and functional disability are unacceptable at the end of 6 to 12 consecutive months of appropriate, active treatment, or at the end of longer duration of non- operative programs for those debilitated with complex problems NOTE:
